From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Close runway + token/unit-econ crosswalk (traffic-sensitive assumptions)

Hi Kevin / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Per our MAP, I put together a focused crosswalk for the remaining econ checks we'll need to sign off the pilot and the contract. The attached workbook (CP-4882_MAP_v1.3.xlsx) has a concise tab called "Econ Checks" but below are the highlights for alignment before Jonas and David run the sim:

Key cost levers we want aligned in the MAP:
- Tokens per session: baseline 1.1k tokens (prompt + average reply). Please confirm expected average message size and frequency during triage flows.
- Cache assumptions: we modeled a 65% prefix/KV cache hit for known-patient flows (warmup + session reuse). If your product keeps conversation context longer the hit rate could be ~80%.
- Batching & microbatching: two profiles in the workbook — low-latency microbatch (batch size 8, target p95 < 180ms) and throughput-optimized batch (batch size 32, p95 ~350ms). Which profile maps to your SLA?
- Reserved capacity buffer: we propose a 20% reserved headroom during launch to avoid throttling-related reroutes.

Asks / next steps for this week:
1) Kevin/Alyssa: confirm product traffic mix (percent of synchronous triage vs async summaries) and average tokens per flow by Mon 23 Jul.
2) Redwood (Jonas + David): run a sensitivity table for tokens/$ showing 3 traffic mixes + cache hit rates 50/65/80% and return a short 2-page readout.
3) Procurement: once econ matrix is acceptable, we'll attach model-level pricing to the MAP and include a 30-day pilot clause.

I've attached a small CSV with the scenario rows we will simulate. If it's helpful, we can also run a short canary profile using sample traffic next week.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

Subject: Re: MAP: Close runway + token/unit-econ crosswalk (traffic-sensitive assumptions)

Priya — thanks, this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic mix: roughly 70% synchronous triage (live chat-like), 20% async clinician summaries, 10% batch exports.
- Average tokens: triage ~900 tokens/session, clinician summaries ~2.8k tokens, batch exports ~12k tokens (but fewer runs).
- Cache behavior: our triage flow reuses a lot of structured context; we believe warm-cache hit should be closer to 72% initially and could reach 78% with a short warm period.
- SLA: p95 latency target for triage must be <250ms. The throughput batch profile is acceptable for background exports.

Procurement: attaching our standard pilot SOW would be helpful to align on the 30-day clause.

If you can run the three-hit-rate sensitivity (50/65/80) with our traffic mix numbers included that would answer the immediate concern for finance. Also, can Redwood show the delta to cost if microbatch size moves from 8 to 16 at the same p95? That's an important trade-off for us.

Kevin

--
Kevin Chan
Head of Product, CarePath Health
kevin.chan@carepath.com | +1 617-555-3420
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Kevin Chan <kevin.chan@carepath.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@carepath.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Close runway + token/unit-econ crosswalk (traffic-sensitive assumptions)

Thanks Kevin — great detail. We'll run the sims with those mix weights. Quick technical notes so the output is actionable for your FinOps team: 

1) Per-route amortization: we'll produce cost-per-conversation and cost-per-API-call rows (so you can see triage vs summary vs export). That separates fixed amortized costs (model load, cold start) from marginal token cost.
2) Cache modeling: our model includes prefix KV cache and a separate session-level cache. The workbook sim will let you toggle both independently.
3) Microbatch trade-off: initial sims will compare batch sizes 8 / 16 / 32 holding target p95 as a soft constraint; we'll show tokens/$ and p95 impact. Historically, shifting 8 -> 16 yields ~18-22% tokens/$ improvement with a small p95 tail increase; exact numbers in the readout.
4) Canary: we can run a 48-hour canary using a 10% traffic mirror from your staging endpoint — this will validate the assumed cache hit rates.

Deliverables and timing:
- Wed 25 Jul EOD: sensitivity matrix (spreadsheet + 1-page TL;DR).
- Fri 27 Jul: optional 48-hour canary (if CarePath signs the data-sharing addendum by Wed).

I'll run sims on a few quantization profiles too (fp16 and 4-bit) so you can see unit-cost vs quality trade-offs.

Jonas

--

Quick update from our side — procurement has the SOW draft and we'll aim to return a countersigned version by Thu EOD. A few notes for the econ sheet peers:

- Please include a "worst-case burst" column where cache drops to 40% (simulates cold-start surge during a campaign). We need to quantify how quickly costs ramp if we lose cache.
- Add a column for "SLA uplift" where we model a 10% premium for guaranteed p95 in the contract (we'd like to see the cost to commit to that).
- For the canary: we'll provide a safe staging mirror; please confirm required logging fields and retention constraints (we cannot share PII outside our VPC).

Thanks everyone — if the sensitivity shows <20% variance across realistic hit rates and batch sizes we can fast-track the pilot sign-off.

Alyssa
